newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Armenian court rejects election challenge.
newsitem.headline: Armenian court rejects election challenge.

text.p: Armenia's Constitutional Court on Friday rejected an opposition plea for the annulment of the results of a presidential election in September, Itar-Tass news agency said.
The decision was likely to fuel tensions in the Armenian capital Yerevan, where opposition supporters have staged big demonstrations against the vote.

The Central Electoral Commission (CEC) declared that President Levon Ter-Petrosyan had won a second five-year term in the September 22 poll, but his election challenger, former prime minister Vazgen Manukyan, accused the president of vote-rigging.
Ter-Petrosyan, a Soviet-era dissident and former close ally of Manukyan in the independence cause, denied the charge.

"The Armenian Constitutional Court turned down a plea by the opposition for the results of the presidential election to be declared invalid," Tass said, quoting the court's chairman, Gagik Arutyunyan.
"The decision is final, is not subject to appeal and comes into force from the moment of publication," he added, according to the agency.
Manukyan had said he doubted that the court, composed of judges appointed by the president and a parliament dominated by the president's bloc, would rule in his favour.

In the immediate aftermath of the election, Ter-Petrosyan sent tanks into the streets, rounded up dozens of opponents, and closed several political parties after demonstrations by Manukyan's backers turned violent.

Foreign observers noted major irregularities in the election by Ter-Petrosyan forces, and the Organisation for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE) said they could have been serious enough to call his victory into question.

The CEC says Ter-Petrosyan, officially sworn in on November 11, won with 51.8 percent of the votes, just clearing the 50-percent hurdle needed to win without a run-off. It said Manukyan won 41.3 percent.
